pending.topic: vLLM V1 Architecture (Decoupled ZeroMQ Engine & GIL Removal)
pending.scenario: Question: How does vLLM V1 compare to Ollama or llama.cpp for local agents?
pending.suggested_reply: Ollama (built on llama.cpp) is great for single-user desktop inference on a laptop. The wall hits when an agent framework spawns 6-10 parallel subagents or tool calls concurrently. vLLM V1's continuous batching + ZeroMQ process isolation keeps token throughput up to 1.7x higher under concurrent load because the HTTP/tokenizer loop never blocks the CUDA scheduler.

pending.topic: vLLM V1 Architecture (Decoupled ZeroMQ Engine & GIL Removal)
pending.scenario: Question: Does ZeroMQ IPC add serialization latency for multimodal inputs?
pending.suggested_reply: For text tokens, ZeroMQ IPC over shared memory adds sub-millisecond overhead, which is completely outweighed by getting tokenization out of the main Python GIL thread. For high-resolution vision frames, V1 caches preprocessed image embeddings so repeated turns in a multi-step trajectory don't re-serialize pixel tensors.

pending.topic: vLLM V1 Architecture (Decoupled ZeroMQ Engine & GIL Removal)
pending.scenario: Question: What GPU specs are realistic for self-hosting V1 in Berlin/EU?
pending.suggested_reply: For 7B to 14B AWQ/FP8 models (like Qwen-2.5-Coder-14B), a single 24GB GPU (RTX 3090/4090 or L4) handles V1 comfortably as long as you cap `--gpu-memory-utilization` at 0.80. Always isolate the server inside a dedicated Docker container with strict memory limits.

pending.topic: DeepSeek Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) & KV Cache Compression
pending.scenario: Question: Do the smaller DeepSeek-R1 distilled models (7B/14B/32B) use MLA?
pending.suggested_reply: That is the biggest catch in practice: the 7B, 14B, 32B, and 70B distilled checkpoints are fine-tuned on top of Qwen-2.5 and Llama-3 backbones, which use standard Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), not native MLA. Only the native DeepSeek-V2/V3/R1-Zero MoE architectures and DeepSeek-Lite use true MLA layers.

pending.topic: DeepSeek Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) & KV Cache Compression
pending.scenario: Question: How does MLA interact with FlashAttention and vLLM/SGLang?
pending.suggested_reply: Standard FlashAttention expects K and V to have the same head dimension, whereas MLA absorbs the up-projection so the latent cache is shared across heads. Both SGLang and vLLM wrote custom FlashMLA / Triton kernels specifically to compute attention directly over the compressed latent cache without materializing full KV tensors.

pending.topic: DeepSeek Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) & KV Cache Compression
pending.scenario: Question: Is KV cache quantization (FP8/INT4) better than MLA?
pending.suggested_reply: They are orthogonal and stackable. Quantizing standard GQA KV cache from FP16 to FP8 gives you a 2x memory reduction. MLA gives you a 5x-13x structural reduction via low-rank matrix factorization first, and you can still store the compressed latent vectors in FP8.

pending.topic: SGLang RadixAttention (Multi-Turn Agent KV Cache Reuse)
pending.scenario: Question: How is SGLang RadixAttention different from Anthropic/OpenAI prompt caching?
pending.suggested_reply: Commercial API prompt caching uses coarse block prefixes and expires after 5-10 minutes of inactivity. SGLang maintains a live LRU Radix Tree in GPU memory that automatically matches arbitrary branching sub-trees across tree-of-thought, parallel tool calls, and multi-turn retries with zero developer annotations.

pending.topic: SGLang RadixAttention (Multi-Turn Agent KV Cache Reuse)
pending.scenario: Question: What happens when the Radix Tree fills up GPU VRAM?
pending.suggested_reply: SGLang evicts leaf nodes first using a Least-Recently-Used (LRU) policy while keeping shared root prefixes (like your core system prompt and tool schemas) pinned in memory as long as active requests reference them.

pending.topic: SGLang RadixAttention (Multi-Turn Agent KV Cache Reuse)
pending.scenario: Question: Does constrained JSON decoding hurt reasoning quality?
pending.suggested_reply: If you force an LLM into a rigid JSON schema on token 1, reasoning quality drops because the model has no scratchpad tokens. In practice, let the model generate an unconstrained `<thinking>` trace first, and apply SGLang's compressed FSM decoding only to the final tool-call payload.

pending.topic: OpenHands (Autonomous Software Engineer inside Docker Sandboxes)
pending.scenario: Question: Can OpenHands run completely offline with local models?
pending.suggested_reply: Yes, you can point it to a local vLLM or Ollama endpoint running Qwen-2.5-Coder-32B. In practice, smaller 7B/8B models struggle with OpenHands' multi-step bash + file-edit action schema, so 32B+ quantized or Claude 3.5 Sonnet is the practical floor for multi-file debugging.

pending.topic: Langfuse (Self-Hosted LLM Observability & Tracing in Docker)
pending.scenario: Question: How heavy is Langfuse v3 with ClickHouse in Docker?
pending.suggested_reply: On a standard 4-vCPU / 8GB RAM Hetzner VPS, the Docker Compose stack runs smoothly for moderate agent workloads, provided you configure a 14-day or 30-day ClickHouse TTL on raw prompt/completion payloads so disk I/O stays predictable.

pending.topic: FastMCP (3-Line Typed Model Context Protocol Servers)
pending.scenario: Question: stdio vs SSE transport for MCP servers in production?
pending.suggested_reply: Use `stdio` for local IDE integrations (VS Code Cline, Cursor, Claude Desktop) because the host process manages lifecycle directly. Use `SSE` or Streamable HTTP inside an isolated Docker container whenever multiple agent workers share the same MCP tool server.

pending.topic: Crawl4AI (Self-Hosted LLM Web Scraper vs Firecrawl)
pending.scenario: Question: How does Crawl4AI handle anti-bot / Cloudflare pages compared to Firecrawl?
pending.suggested_reply: Crawl4AI supports stealth browser flags, custom user agents, and residential proxy rotation out of the box. For internal documentation, public technical docs, and arXiv/GitHub scraping, local headless Chromium handles 95% of targets at $0 API cost.

pending.topic: Pydantic AI (Typed Dependency Injection vs Prompt Guessing)
pending.scenario: Question: Why use Pydantic AI over LangChain / LangGraph?
pending.suggested_reply: Zero hidden prompt wrappers and standard Python type checking with mypy/pyright. Your agent tools look and test exactly like FastAPI endpoints, making unit testing with mock dependencies trivial.

pending.scenario: Question: Best architect + editor model pairing in Aider?
pending.suggested_reply: Pairing DeepSeek-R1 or Claude 3.5 Sonnet as the Architect model with Qwen-2.5-Coder-32B as the fast Editor model cuts token spend by ~50% while maintaining top SWE-bench edit accuracy.

pending.scenario: Question: MarkItDown vs Docling for complex PDFs?
pending.suggested_reply: MarkItDown is ultra-lightweight and fast for Office formats (.docx, .pptx, .xlsx) and digital-native PDFs. For complex multi-column scanned scientific PDFs with bounding-box layout analysis, IBM's open-source Docling is stronger.

pending.scenario: Question: How do you sandbox a desktop GUI agent safely?
pending.suggested_reply: Run the entire Xvfb / VNC desktop session inside an isolated Docker container or QEMU VM with outbound network rules restricted to whitelisted domains.
